statement: On a small site T [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let B be a commutative ring. There is an isomorphism e from the ring underlying the constant commutative-ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension] to the constant ring sheaf, intertwining the two constant-presheaf sheafification units [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every module sheaf F over the first ring, local constant finite-module descriptions [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules] hold for F if and only if the old constant-ring descriptions [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf] hold after restricting along e inverse. The unit compatibility determines the isomorphism uniquely; the proof constructs it by the canonical constant-sheaf comparison.

proof.text: Forgetting commutativity preserves locally injective and locally surjective maps because underlying functions are unchanged. The characterization of sheafification equivalences by local bijectivity therefore shows that it preserves sheafification. Mathlib constantCommuteCompose gives the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism, and its formula together with sheafComposeIso_inv_fac and naturality of toSheafify gives the compatibility with units. The isomorphism is explicitly constructed, not selected from an unproved existence statement.

For an abstract ring isomorphism satisfying this unit compatibility, the module-sheafification adjunction constructs the comparison between the old constant module sheaf and inverse scalar restriction of the new one. On associated additive-group sheaves it is the identity, so it is an isomorphism.

Scalar restriction commutes with slices. In one direction restrict each local constant trivialization and apply the constant-module comparison. In the other, apply scalar restriction along the inverse map and use the explicit cancellation isomorphisms, built sectionwise from ordinary module restriction. The same finite B-module is used in either direction.

theorem exists_constantCoefficientRing_localModels_comparison
    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] (T : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] :
    ∃ e : constantCoefficientRing T B ≅ (constantSheaf T RingCat.{u}).obj (RingCat.of B),
      (constantCoefficientUnit T B ≫ e.hom.hom =
        toSheafify T ((Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj (RingCat.of B))) ∧
      ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (constantCoefficientRing T B),
        IsLocallyConstantFiniteTypeModules T B F ↔
          IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant T B ((restrictScalars e.inv).obj F)
